newsitem.title: USA: Motorola unveils new two-way pager.
newsitem.headline: Motorola unveils new two-way pager.

text.p: Motorola Inc. on Tuesday unveiled its pocket-sized two-way pager which allows users to send electronic mail, faxes and messages to other pagers.

With a miniature keyboard that unfolds from the pager, the PageWriter allows the user to create and send messages without hooking up to a phone or computer, like previous two-way pagers have required.

Like traditional pagers, PageWriter is small enough to wear and receives numeric and text messages over paging frequencies. It is slightly larger than a deck of cards and weighs approximately 6.3 ounces.
The Schaumburg, Ill.-based company said PageWriter will be undergoing extensive beta testing through the end of the year and is expected to be commercially available the first half of 1997.

"It has a whole new feature set and is clearly unique," said John Lazlo, an analyst for Paine Webber. "There is a part of the pager market that relies on having messages downloaded and being able to answer them."
PageWriter will be available directly from Motorola for $399 and through various paging service providers at the prices they determine.
